subject: Model shortlist & context-sizing for Helix Health deployment

Subject: Initial: model shortlist + context sizing for Helix Health deployment

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed. Attached is our RFP snapshot and an abbreviated usage sample. We need help narrowing a model shortlist and establishing a realistic token/throughput budget for our pilot (clinical summarization and triage assistant). High-level requirements: 
- Expected concurrent users in pilot: 30–50 (clinicians + triage nurses); production target: 500 DAU
- Typical prompt length (patient notes + rubrics): 600–2,000 tokens; generation outputs average 150–400 tokens
- Soft latency target: 500ms p95 for short queries (<=512 tokens), 1.2s p95 for longer ones
- Compliance: PHI; must run in a dedicated environment or Redwood Private

Questions:
1) Which models should we shortlist for accuracy/latency tradeoffs given the above context windows?
2) What initial monthly token budget do you recommend for the pilot vs. production ramp?
3) Any immediate red flags in the RFP or the sample payloads?

Can we get a short note back by end of week? I cc'd procurement with timeline expectations.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Kim
Head of Clinical Product, Helix Health

Subject: Re: Initial: model shortlist + context sizing for Helix Health deployment

Hi Andrew — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP. Short answers up front, then a short proposal we can iterate on: 

1) Model shortlist (pilot -> production progression):
   - Pilot (fast iteration, lower infra cost): Mistral-Instruct-7B q4_0 (good instruction following, smaller KV footprint)
   - Pilot (higher-quality option): Llama2-13B-Chat 8k (better long-context coherence at modest cost)
   - Production candidate (if you need RLHF safety/clinical tuning): Redwood-Align-13B or a quantized 30B variant with guardrails

2) Context lengths: request windows you listed (600–2k) are within a 4k context comfortably. We recommend starting pilot at a 4k context window to avoid early truncation and reserve 8k/16k testing for escalations (e.g., long longitudinal notes).

3) Token budget (rough):
   - Pilot (3 months): assume 50 concurrent active users, avg 8 interactions/day, avg prompt 1,200 tokens, avg generation 250 tokens => 50 * 8 * (1,200+250) * 30 days ≈ 51.75M tokens/month peak.
   - Production (500 DAU ramp): 500 * 10 * (1,200+300) * 30 ≈ 1.98B tokens/month.

Notes: these estimates are conservative (assume clinician workflows have heavier context). We'll provide a per-route breakdown and batchable opportunities to reduce cost (prefix caching of patient histories, response caching for repeated templates).

Action items proposed:
- Vivek: provide latency/throughput estimates for shortlisted models on Dedicated (Nvidia H100/4xA100 configs) and suggestion for quantization.
- Laura: will draft a 6-week mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones for pilot rollout, security checklist for Private deployment, and procurement handoff steps.
- Monica: I'll loop you in for onboarding checkpoints and CS success metrics.

I'll attach our benchmark CSV and a quick model-comparison slide. Let us know if you prefer Private vs Dedicated for the pilot — given PHI, Private or Dedicated reserved capacity is recommended.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial: model shortlist + context sizing for Helix Health deployment

Andrew — quick technical read on Sergio's initial shortlist and token assumptions. A few points to consider: 

- Context & caching: For clinical summaries with recurring patient histories, prefix (KV) caching can cut prompt tokens by 30–60% if you store the static patient background and only send deltas per request. We'll prototype a cache key based on patient_id + encounter_id.
- Model latency & throughput: On Dedicated (4 x A100 80GB) we expect:
   * Mistral-Instruct-7B q4: p95 generation for 400-token outputs ~ 220–300ms (batch=8)
   * Llama2-13B chat (float16): p95 ~ 420–650ms (batch=4)
   * Quantized 30B variant: p95 ~ 850–1,200ms depending on kernel support
- Quantization tradeoffs: q4_0 is a good starting point; it reduces memory by ~55% with ~1–3% EM loss on instruction metrics. For clinical tasks we prefer a small eval set before switching to aggressive quantization.
- Autoscale & SLOs: Given your p95 targets, we recommend a Dedicated pool sized for steady-state throughput + 2x burst for clinic peak hours (11am-2pm). We'll provide an autoscale policy draft in the MAP.

I'll prepare a short performance matrix (latency vs cost) for the options and include expected tokens-per-second per GPU for each model.

Vivek
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Week 6: pilot review & go/no-go decision
